items.title: The US military’s race to make fake blood
items.raw_text: Its call sign was Morphine 1-2. In February 2007, the hulking dual-­rotor casualty evacuation helicopter had just flown three wounded soldiers to a field hospital in Balad, north of Baghdad, when another call came: an emergency mission to fly through an insurgent-controlled area in broad daylight. Typically, helicopters would be in a spot like this only at night, and with all lights turned off. As it passed near the city of Karmah, in the eastern side of Al-Anbar province, an insurgent fired a portable missile launcher. The tail gunner, who likely saw the shot roaring in, yelled for the pilot to make an evasive move. But the missile had already locked on, and the ensuing blast started a fire on board. After the pilot battled the failing machine for 58 agonizing seconds, Morphine 1-2 plunged to the ground. All seven crew members were killed. Why was the helo there in daylight? “It was getting blood and bringing it back. It was [on] what we call a ‘blood run,’ and [it’s] the highest of priorities besides casualty evacuation,” explains Lieutenant Commander Robert Murray, a Navy officer and program manager at DARPA, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, who studied this incident as an intelligence officer. Today, a chronic shortage of blood in both the military and civilian worlds is fueling a race to develop synthetic alternatives. items.raw_text: Redesigning source control at Anthropic Interesting piece from Anthropic describing why and how they built their own custom alternative to Git, based on the dramatic increase in rate of changes to their code after the past six months. In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day. They included a chart showing those changes. I had Claude modify their chart ( code here ) to add markers for the public releases of each of their models in 2026: This shows public release dates, not the date when models became available for Anthropic's internal use. My guess is that the introduction of Fable/Mythos class models is a key factor in the increased coding velocity. "Antique" is their new code review system. The source control system is called Scion, and sounds to me like a reinvention of centralized source control along the lines of Subversion. They had some pretty extreme requirements: The history of our main branch alone is almost 100 GB, and a compressed working copy is over 25 GB. We perform on the order of 25 million code checkouts per day for CI, before counting developer environments, agent sandboxes, and research jobs. Fetched naively, that would be over 600 PB of git traffic per day. The new system was built by a team of seven people, and the migration from Git was completed in five months. items.title: In Memoriam: Jan Ewout van der Putten
items.raw_text: Op 30 september 2026 overleed Jan Ewout van der Putten, 78 jaar oud. Als secretaris-directeur van eerst de Vereniging NBLC en later de Vereniging van Openbare Bibliotheken was hij bijna elf jaar nauw betrokken bij de ontwikkeling van het Nederlandse openbare bibliotheekwerk. Samenwerking en inhoudelijke vernieuwing stonden daarbij voor hem voorop. Tekst: Eimer Wieldraaijer Toen Van der Putten in februari 1999 aantrad bij de Vereniging NBLC, bracht hij een ruime bestuurlijke ervaring mee. Hij was tien jaar plaatsvervangend griffier van de Eerste Kamer geweest en vervolgens zes jaar wethouder voor D66 in Den Haag. Hij kende de politieke besluitvorming van binnenuit: een waardevolle achtergrond voor een sector waarin gemeenten, provincies en rijksoverheid ieder hun eigen verantwoordelijkheden en belangen hadden. Zijn directeurschap viel samen met een ingrijpende periode van bibliotheekvernieuwing. De vorming van basisbibliotheken, veranderende bestuurlijke verhoudingen en de ontwikkeling van digitale dienstverlening vroegen om richting en afstemming. Van der Putten behoorde tot de landelijke hoofdrolspelers in dat proces. Ook droeg hij bij aan een nieuwe structuur voor het blindenbibliotheekwerk en de verbinding daarvan met het reguliere openbare bibliotheekwerk. Toegankelijkheid kreeg zo een concrete organisatorische vertaling. Zijn werkterrein reikte bovendien verder dan Nederland. items.title: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
items.raw_text: When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money. He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around $15,000) for the workspace data in Google, Notion, Figma, and Slack. “At least all that stuff we were doing for two and a half years is worth something to someone somewhere,” he says. The sale was brokered by a company called SimpleClosure, part of a new growth sector in tech: businesses catering to dying startups. Estimates from Carta and AngelList show shutdowns rising between 26% and 56% annually in recent years, and an end-of-life ecosystem—including coaches, “death doulas,” and firms that help handle the legal, tax, and operational headaches of going ­belly-up—has emerged. Now tech undertakers are selling the data remains to AI labs. SimpleClosure added data sales to its services in April. Its Asset Hub platform helps founders sell their code and workspace data—emails, chats, documents. Buyers include foundation AI labs, vendors that construct simulated workspaces for AI training, and mature tech companies building their own models. items.title: Metropolitan Libraries Spotlight: How Nanhai Library Is Reconnecting Children with the Classics
items.raw_text: When a thousand-year-old novel has to compete with a 15-second video In Foshan, in the heart of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, Nanhai Library serves a district of more than 3.7 million people, where local families, migrant workers, students, and seniors intertwine in a fast-moving, diverse community. It is also a community facing a very contemporary problem: as short-form video quietly absorbs every spare moment of screen time, deep reading is being pushed to the margins, even when the content at stake is centuries old. Rather than treat this as a lost cause, the library decided to meet children where their attention already lives. In April 2026, it launched Classics 101: Mental Models for Kids, a program built specifically for 10- to 12-year-olds — the exact age when children move from picture-to-text bridge books into more demanding reading. Making the classics legible again The challenge was concrete and specific. More than 60% of students in the first sessions admitted their biggest frustration was simple: they could not remember who everyone was or how all the characters connected. The semi-archaic language, sprawling character webs, and unhurried pacing of China’s Four Great Classical Novels were never designed to compete with instant gratification. So Nanhai Library stopped asking children to memorize plots and started extracting something more useful: practical mental models drawn directly from the characters’ journeys. items.title: Show HN: Parsimony – an open-source benchmark for how much code AI models add
items.raw_text: Existing benchmarks measure solve rate and token output/cost, but don't punish excess code, which makes a codebase harder to work with in the long term. I wanted to measure this since it matters most for long-term projects. Method: it takes the patches that benchmarks already publish (DeepSWE, SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Live) and counts "coding units": syntax elements like statements, calls, names and literals. I didn't use lines of code, so cramming code isn't rewarded. Deleted code is subtracted, so it measures net units. GPT-6 and Claude 5.5 have no public patches yet, so I ran them myself on 3–10 tasks on my own subscriptions (shown as faded circles, not ranked). Any feedback or model contributions are welcome, especially public patch exports for newer models. GitHub: https://github.com/La5u/Parsimony Not affiliated with any of the benchmarks.

The big trade shows for cars were a gateway drug for many, expos where you could see the newest models of today and the concepts of tomorrow. But automakers increasingly got tired of sharing the spotlight with each other. New reveals moved offsite to events the night or even the week before the show itself. One by one, brands pulled out of auto show after auto show until there was little left to see . And then the pandemic hit. But the news out of Paris, where its auto show held media day yesterday, seems like we stepped back into a time when automakers would debut new cars aplenty. That retro vibe extends to the cars themselves, with plenty of familiar nameplates reimagined. France’s Renault has a long and glorious history of delightful concept cars, and more on what it brought to Paris later. But the star of the show was arguably Stellantis, with strong work from Citroen, Peugeot, and Fiat, to name but three. items.title: High-speed video reveals how honey bee stingers pump venom
items.raw_text: Credit: Ramirez-Esquivel et al 202 Credit: Ramirez-Esquivel et al 202 Honey bees are known to leave their stingers embedded in tender flesh once they sting you and fly away. Scientists have now determined that the stinger is able to continue pumping venom into its unfortunate victim even after the bee flies away, thanks to a unique double-piston pump-like mechanism, according to a new paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Different species have evolved different mechanisms for delivering venom, which involves piercing the skin and then pumping venom from a gland or reservoir. Spiders, for instance, have muscles surrounding their venom glands, which contract and eject venom through hollow fangs. Bees, wasps, and ants deliver venom via their stingers, either by contracting muscles around the venom reservoir or through stiff elements called lancets working together to pump venom. Honey bees ( Apis mellifera ) add a unique feature: Worker bees fly away after inserting their stingers in the target, leaving the stinger behind. The stinger continues to penetrate the tissue and pump venom on its own, a rare phenomenon known as autotomy. A honey bee's stinger has three main interlocking elements that form the venom canal: a stylet that widens to form the main pumping chamber and two sharp-tipped lancets that slide back and forth, piercing the tissue and pumping venom into the target. Long-lost horror gaming cult classic P.T. gets a much-needed PC port
items.raw_text: For over a decade now, the only "official" way to play Hideo Kojima's cult classic, P.T. —the long-discontinued "playable trailer" for Kojima's canceled "Silent Hills" project —has been via one of the increasingly rare PlayStation 4s that previously downloaded a copy during its monthslong availability window. Now, though, one coder is helping to preserve the game with a porting tool that builds a playable x86 PC executable from the original PS4 files. Coder Lorean Xavier said he was inspired to work on the "P.T. for PC" project "because P.T. deserved to keep existing somewhere other than on consoles that still have it installed." The open source porting effort rebuilds the P.T. engine in C++ and Vulkan, using the original files from the PS4 game to re-create "every level, model, texture, sound, script and cutscene," according to its GitHub listing. That means players without their own legitimate decrypted copy of the original P.T. will have to track one down in order to generate a playable PC version. The reliance on real P.T. files makes this port more authentic than previous hobbyist efforts to re-create the look and feel of P.T. for a PC audience. And while PS4 emulators recently reached a point where they could run P.T. completely , this native port also sports extra features, like upscaling and frame-generation, a camera mode, experimental third-person and VR support, and a "museum" section where you can look at and listen to in-game assets (including "unused content").

As tracks go, the 90-degree turns and concrete barrier-lined streets were a world away from the abrasive tarmac and ample runoff of Malaysia last time out . items.title: Rechtszaak tegen Apple over scraping van YouTube-video’s gaat door
items.raw_text: Apple moet zich voor de rechter verantwoorden voor beschuldigingen dat het bedrijf YouTube-video’s zonder toestemming heeft verzameld om generatieve AI-modellen te trainen. Die modellen kunnen op basis van tekstbeschrijvingen video’s genereren. Een Amerikaanse federale rechter heeft besloten dat de rechtszaak mag doorgaan. De zaak is aangespannen door Ted Entertainment, het bedrijf achter verschillende YouTube-kanalen, waaronder h3h3 Productions, en Matt Fisher, die golfvideo’s publiceert via het kanaal MrShortGame Golf. Zij beschuldigen Apple ervan de Amerikaanse Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) te hebben overtreden. Deze wet verbiedt onder meer het omzeilen van technische beveiligingsmaatregelen die de toegang tot digitale content reguleren. Volgens de aanklagers gebruikte Apple geautomatiseerde programma’s om video’s te downloaden. Daarbij zouden virtuele machines zijn ingezet die regelmatig van IP-adres wisselden om detectie en blokkades te voorkomen. Op die manier zou het bedrijf op grote schaal ongeoorloofd toegang hebben gekregen tot video’s. Apple probeerde de zaak in een vroeg stadium te laten afwijzen. Het bedrijf voerde aan dat YouTube-video’s openbaar toegankelijk zijn en dat het downloaden daarvan daarom niet automatisch betekent dat technische toegangsbeveiligingen zijn omzeild. Rechter Richard Seeborg verwierp dat argument. Volgens hem beperken de technische maatregelen van YouTube de toegang tot het platform en de daarvoor bedoelde streamingtechnologie.

items.title: Nederlands MKB ziet AI als productiemiddel, geen groeimotor
items.raw_text: Marketeers in het Nederlandse MKB gebruiken AI vooral als versneller van het maakwerk, niet als vehikel voor algemene groeiversnelling van de organisatie. Dat blijkt uit een onderzoeksrapport van digitaal bureau Fingerspitz . Driekwart van de bedrijven zet AI-tools in voor marketing, maar slechts zes procent werkt met agents, eigen modellen of diepe integraties in de eigen systemen. Het gebruik is breed, maar de diepgang is gering. Het patroon zit in wat de tools precies doen. Het blijkt dat vooral het laaghangende fruit wordt geplukt met AI’s. Ondernemers gebruiken AI voor brainstormen (61 procent), copywriting (58 procent) en visuals (47 procent). Data-analyse haalt 42 procent en campagne-optimalisatie en targeting, de plekken waar AI doorgaans het meest rendement belooft, blijven steken op twintig procent. Van de ondervraagden betaalt 22 procent niets voor AI-tools en 36 procent minder dan honderd euro per maand. Bij 51 procent zijn geen specifieke budgetten toegewezen voor AI-marketingtools en -trainingen. Die kosten verdwijnen in het algemene budget voor marketingsoftware.
